name: su
summary: Opens a shell as another user.
description: Switch user: changes identity in the terminal. Unlike sudo, su asks for the TARGET user’s password (root’s for a plain su). On Ubuntu, the root account has no password by default: use sudo -i or sudo su instead. Type exit to go back to your own account.

options.description: Login shell: loads the target user’s full environment (home directory, variables). Same as “su -”.
Runs a single command as the user, then comes back.
Uses this shell instead of the target user’s.

arguments.name: USER
arguments.description: Account to use. Default: root. A lone dash before the name (su - name) loads their full environment.

examples.explanation: Becomes root with root’s environment (root’s password is asked for).
Opens a session as alice, in her home directory.
Runs a single command as root.
Becomes postgres with your own password, thanks to sudo.

dangerNote: As root, nothing stops you from damaging the system. Leave the root shell (exit) as soon as you are done.
